races.title: State Senate, District 47
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ralph Hise
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 47 since 2011, from Spruce Pine. Served as Deputy President Pro Tempore of the NC Senate beginning in 2019. Statistician by training, with a master's in higher education administration. Has worked at Mayland Community College and as an Expert-in-Residence at UNC-Asheville's Health Policy Institute.

controversies.text: In 2017 an activist complained to the State Board of Elections that Hise's campaign repaid him about $10,000 more than he had loaned it. In November 2018 the board settled the matter. His campaign paid a $500 fine and $4,000 for investigation costs. His lawyer said the cause was bookkeeping and reporting errors, not improper payments.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Hise on data centers, development and land use, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, police pay, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. His campaign site says he has worked to lower taxes, but it gives no homestead-specific pledge or bill. We could not establish when his campaign site was last updated; its copyright says 2022. We found no official statement on how the 2017 campaign finance complaints were resolved.

local.label: Roots 100: He is described as a native of Mitchell County, attended Mitchell High School there, and still lives in Spruce Pine.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2011 and Deputy President Pro Tempore of the Senate from 2019. Statistician by training, with work at Mayland Community College and a health-policy post at UNC-Asheville.
qual.why: More than 15 years of legislative service and a chamber leadership post, together with a statistics and policy background, put him in the high band. Committee chair roles were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he is a "staunch defender of the 2nd amendment" who will oppose attempts to erode it, and it cites an A rating from the NRA.

cands.name: Frank Patton Hughes III
cands.bio: Public high school social studies teacher in McDowell County, lead world history teacher at McDowell High School. Earlier taught in Winston-Salem. Chair of the Avery County Democratic Party. Democratic nominee for NC Senate District 47 in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter guide recommendation from the 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' Sway voting group (Vote for Peace).
Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter guide recommendation from the 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' Sway voting group (Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: He has never held public office, so there is no voting or legislative record to review. We found no independent news coverage of him, so his biography comes from his own campaign site and Ballotpedia survey. We found no stated positions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B visas, policing, gun laws or abortion. His statements on growth and land protection are general (protecting forests, rivers and farms) with no specific policy. The data center statements are undated and do not say whether he would ban or pause them. No controversies or foreign ties were found.

local.label: Roots 100: He says he was born in Iredell County, NC, attended school in Avery and Guilford counties, and has spent most of his life in Avery County.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Public school teacher (high school world history and social studies, lead teacher roles), and one of three writers and advisors of an eighth-grade social studies curriculum for Winston-Salem/Forsyth schools. Earlier jobs include landscape nurseryman and car mechanic. Chairs the Avery County Democratic Party. No elected office or legislative or budget work found.
qual.why: His record is a teaching career with some curriculum work. No prior legislative service, elected office, or law, policy or budget career was found, so he falls in the lower band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: His record is a teaching career with some curriculum work. No prior legislative service, elected office, or law, policy or budget career was found, so he falls in the lower band for writing law and the state budget.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Campaign site says he stands firmly against the unregulated expansion of data centers that he says strain the grid, raise utility bills and strip local communities of their voice. He also says he is not anti-innovation. He does not call for a statewide ban or moratorium.

clean-money.evidence: Campaign site notes that the incumbent accepts contributions from Duke Energy and says of himself, 'I will not.'

Says data centers 'strain our grid, drain our water' and he 'will not support systems that take advantage of the people in North Carolina.'
